programme.displayName: Amazon DynamoDB: Build a Resilient Serverless Orders Data Store
programme.subtitle: Create, query, protect, replicate, monitor, and safely remove a DynamoDB orders workload.
programme.description: Start with no training infrastructure and build a complete DynamoDB orders data store in eu-west-2. Create a dedicated IAM user and named CLI profile, design a composite primary key with an LSI and GSI, practise safe writes and efficient reads, configure TTL and Streams, prove backup recovery, test multi-Region Global Tables replication, and remove every training resource.
programme.learningOutcome: Build and explain a secure, serverless DynamoDB design using the Console and AWS CLI; select efficient keys and indexes; distinguish Query from Scan; use conditional updates, TTL, Streams, PITR, backups, and Global Tables; apply SAA-C03 architecture decisions; and complete exact reverse-order cleanup.

tasks.title: Create the training identity and configure AWS CLI access
tasks.goal: Use an administrator only for bootstrap, then complete the lab as the dedicated fa-dynamodb-user in eu-west-2.
tasks.whyItMatters: SAA-C03 expects least privilege, non-root administration, and clear separation between human credentials and workload roles.

consoleSteps.title: Create the customer-managed training policy
consoleSteps.instruction: Sign in with an existing administrator-capable identity; do not use the root user for routine lab work.

instructions.text: Sign in with an existing administrator-capable identity; do not use the root user for routine lab work.
Open the IAM console from the AWS Console search bar.
In the left navigation, choose Policies.
Choose Create policy.
Choose the JSON editor.
Replace <ACCOUNT_ID> in the supplied policy with the 12-digit account ID shown in the Console account menu.
Replace the editor content with the complete policy JSON below.
Choose Next.
Enter fa-dynamodb-training-policy as the policy name.
Review that table access is limited to names beginning fa-dynamodb-.
Choose Create policy.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: IAM shows fa-dynamodb-training-policy as a customer-managed policy.
consoleSteps.warning: This is a temporary training policy. Do not paste credentials into the policy or broaden its resources to every DynamoDB table.

consoleSteps.title: Create the training user, attach the policy, and create one access key
consoleSteps.instruction: In IAM, choose Users.

instructions.text: In IAM, choose Users.
Choose Create user.
Enter fa-dynamodb-user.
Enable AWS Management Console access for this training user.
Set a temporary password using your normal secure password procedure.
Require the learner to create a new password at the next sign-in.
Choose Next.
Choose Attach policies directly.
Search for fa-dynamodb-training-policy.
Select only fa-dynamodb-training-policy.
Choose Next and then Create user.
Open fa-dynamodb-user.
Choose the Security credentials tab.
In Access keys, choose Create access key.
Choose Command Line Interface (CLI) as the use case and acknowledge the recommendation.
Choose Create access key.
Record the access key ID as [FA_DYNAMODB_ACCESS_KEY_ID] and store the secret access key securely; AWS shows the secret only once.
Sign out of the administrator session.
Use the IAM-user sign-in URL to sign in as fa-dynamodb-user.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The Console identity is fa-dynamodb-user and exactly one active access key exists for it.
consoleSteps.warning: Never paste the secret access key into Author, the Follow Along, source control, screenshots, or chat.

consoleSteps.title: Select the lab Region and confirm DynamoDB access
consoleSteps.instruction: In the top navigation Region selector, choose Europe (London) eu-west-2.

instructions.text: In the top navigation Region selector, choose Europe (London) eu-west-2.
Search for DynamoDB and open it.
Choose Tables in the left navigation.
Confirm the page loads without AccessDenied.
Do not select or change any pre-existing table.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The DynamoDB Tables page is open in Europe (London) and no existing resource was changed.
consoleSteps.warning: Every regional command and Console action in this lab must remain in eu-west-2 unless the Global Tables task explicitly says eu-west-1.

cliSteps.command: aws iam create-policy --policy-name fa-dynamodb-training-policy --policy-document file://fa-dynamodb-training-policy.json --profile [ADMIN_PROFILE]
cliSteps.explanation: After saving the displayed policy JSON and replacing <ACCOUNT_ID>, an existing administrator creates the scoped customer-managed policy.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response contains PolicyName fa-dynamodb-training-policy and its ARN.
cliSteps.warning: Run this only with an existing administrator profile. IAM is global, so --region is intentionally omitted.

cliSteps.command: aws iam create-user --user-name fa-dynamodb-user --profile [ADMIN_PROFILE]
cliSteps.explanation: The administrator creates the dedicated training user.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response contains UserName fa-dynamodb-user.
cliSteps.warning: Do not run this with root access keys.

cliSteps.command: aws iam attach-user-policy --user-name fa-dynamodb-user --policy-arn arn:aws:iam::<ACCOUNT_ID>:policy/fa-dynamodb-training-policy --profile [ADMIN_PROFILE]
cliSteps.explanation: This attaches only the training policy to the new user.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command returns without an error.
cliSteps.warning: Replace <ACCOUNT_ID> with the account ID before running the command.

cliSteps.command: aws iam create-access-key --user-name fa-dynamodb-user --profile [ADMIN_PROFILE]
cliSteps.explanation: The administrator creates one programmatic access key for the training user.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The output contains an AccessKeyId and SecretAccessKey; record the ID as [FA_DYNAMODB_ACCESS_KEY_ID].
cliSteps.warning: The secret is shown once. Configure it immediately and never save it in the repository.

cliSteps.command: aws configure --profile fa-dynamodb
cliSteps.explanation: Enter the new training access key ID, its secret, eu-west-2, and json at the four prompts.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The named profile fa-dynamodb is created locally.
cliSteps.warning: Do not paste credential values into any command argument or documentation.

cliSteps.command: aws sts get-caller-identity --profile fa-dynamodb
cliSteps.explanation: This proves which identity the CLI will use before any resource is created.
cliSteps.expectedResult: Arn ends with user/fa-dynamodb-user and Account contains the expected 12-digit account ID.
cliSteps.warning: Stop if the ARN shows root, a different user, or an unexpected account.

cliSteps.command: aws dynamodb list-tables --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-dynamodb
cliSteps.explanation: This verifies DynamoDB discovery access in the correct Region.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command returns a TableNames array without AccessDenied.
cliSteps.warning: Do not operate on any table not beginning fa-dynamodb-.

verification.title: Confirm the Console identity
verification.instruction: Open the account menu and confirm the signed-in user is fa-dynamodb-user.
verification.expectedResult: The root user and administrator are no longer used for normal lab work.

verification.title: Confirm the CLI identity and Region
verification.instruction: Run the caller-identity check and inspect the fa-dynamodb profile Region.
verification.expectedResult: The identity is fa-dynamodb-user and the Region is eu-west-2.

verification.title: Confirm scoped discovery
verification.instruction: Open DynamoDB Tables or list tables without changing any existing table.
verification.expectedResult: DynamoDB discovery succeeds and no unrelated table is modified.

tasks.title: Create the orders table with a composite key, LSI, and GSI
tasks.goal: Create one on-demand DynamoDB table whose keys support customer, time, and order-status access patterns.
tasks.whyItMatters: DynamoDB designs begin with access patterns. Partition-key distribution, sort-key ordering, and choosing GSI versus LSI are frequent SAA-C03 decisions.

consoleSteps.title: Create the base table and primary key
consoleSteps.instruction: Open DynamoDB in Europe (London) eu-west-2.

instructions.text: Open DynamoDB in Europe (London) eu-west-2.
Choose Tables.
Choose Create table.
Enter fa-dynamodb-orders for Table name.
Enter customerId for Partition key and keep String selected.
Enter orderId for Sort key and keep String selected.
In Table settings, choose Customize settings.
For Table class, keep DynamoDB Standard.
For Capacity mode, choose On-demand.
Keep the default AWS owned key encryption option.
Keep deletion protection off because this temporary table must be removed during final cleanup.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The form shows customerId as the partition key, orderId as the sort key, and On-demand capacity.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not reuse the name of an existing learner-owned table.

consoleSteps.title: Add the local and global secondary indexes before creation
consoleSteps.instruction: In Secondary indexes, choose Create local index.

instructions.text: In Secondary indexes, choose Create local index.
Enter createdAt as the LSI sort key with String type.
Enter customer-createdAt-index as the index name.
Keep All attributes projected and save the local index.
Choose Create global index.
Enter status as the GSI partition key with String type.
Enter createdAt as the GSI sort key with String type.
Enter status-createdAt-index as the index name.
Keep All attributes projected and save the global index.
In Tags, add Project with value fa-dynamodb-training.
Review the settings and choose Create table.
Wait until Table status changes from Creating to Active.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: fa-dynamodb-orders is Active with customer-createdAt-index and status-createdAt-index.
consoleSteps.warning: An LSI can only be defined when its base table is created; do not continue if the LSI is missing.

cliSteps.command: aws dynamodb create-table --cli-input-json file://fa-dynamodb-orders-table.json --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-dynamodb
cliSteps.explanation: Save the displayed table specification as fa-dynamodb-orders-table.json. It creates the on-demand table, both indexes, encryption, and the training tag in one request.
cliSteps.expectedResult: TableDescription.TableStatus is CREATING.
cliSteps.warning: Do not run this if fa-dynamodb-orders already exists.

cliSteps.command: aws dynamodb wait table-exists --table-name fa-dynamodb-orders --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-dynamodb
cliSteps.explanation: DynamoDB table creation is asynchronous, so this waits for the table to become usable.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The waiter exits successfully.
cliSteps.warning: Wait for this command before writing any items.

cliSteps.command: aws dynamodb describe-table --table-name fa-dynamodb-orders --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-dynamodb
cliSteps.explanation: The description exposes table status, key schema, billing mode, indexes, encryption, and ARN.
cliSteps.expectedResult: TableStatus is ACTIVE; BillingModeSummary is PAY_PER_REQUEST; both named indexes appear.

verification.title: Verify the primary key
verification.instruction: Open the Overview tab for fa-dynamodb-orders.
verification.expectedResult: Partition key is customerId (String) and sort key is orderId (String).

verification.title: Verify both index types
verification.instruction: Open the Indexes tab or inspect describe-table.
verification.expectedResult: customer-createdAt-index is an LSI and status-createdAt-index is a GSI; both are ACTIVE.

verification.title: Verify capacity and encryption
verification.instruction: Inspect Additional settings or the table description.
verification.expectedResult: Capacity is On-demand and server-side encryption is enabled with an AWS owned key.

tasks.title: Load harmless orders and understand item structure
tasks.goal: Create three typed DynamoDB items and retrieve one item by its full primary key.
tasks.whyItMatters: DynamoDB items are schemaless beyond their keys, but attribute types, item size, and exact primary-key values determine application correctness.

consoleSteps.title: Create the three training items in JSON view
consoleSteps.instruction: Open DynamoDB and choose Explore table items.

instructions.text: Open DynamoDB and choose Explore table items.
Select fa-dynamodb-orders.
Choose Create item.
Choose JSON view.
Replace the editor content with the first supplied order JSON and choose Create item.
Repeat Create item and JSON view for the second supplied order JSON.
Repeat Create item and JSON view for the third supplied order JSON.
Return to Items returned and choose Run to refresh the list.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: Three harmless order items are visible: ORDER#1001, ORDER#1002, and ORDER#2001.
consoleSteps.warning: Use the DynamoDB attribute-value JSON shown below; do not insert customer names, email addresses, payment data, or other personal information.

consoleSteps.title: Retrieve one exact order
consoleSteps.instruction: In Explore table items, change the operation from Scan to Query.

instructions.text: In Explore table items, change the operation from Scan to Query.
Select Table as the query target.
Enter CUSTOMER#100 for customerId.
Add the orderId sort-key condition Equals.
Enter ORDER#1001.
Choose Run.
Expand the returned item and inspect each attribute type.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: Exactly one item is returned with status PENDING and amount 49.99.
consoleSteps.warning: DynamoDB number attributes are represented as numbers in the Console and as N strings in low-level CLI JSON.

cliSteps.command: aws dynamodb put-item --table-name fa-dynamodb-orders --item file://order-1001.json --condition-expression "attribute_not_exists(customerId) AND attribute_not_exists(orderId)" --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-dynamodb
cliSteps.explanation: Save the first displayed item document as order-1001.json. The condition prevents accidental replacement of the same key.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command succeeds with no response body.
cliSteps.warning: If ConditionalCheckFailedException appears, stop and inspect the existing item instead of overwriting it.

cliSteps.command: aws dynamodb put-item --table-name fa-dynamodb-orders --item file://order-1002.json --condition-expression "attribute_not_exists(customerId) AND attribute_not_exists(orderId)" --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-dynamodb
cliSteps.explanation: This writes the second order for CUSTOMER#100.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command succeeds with no response body.
cliSteps.warning: Do not remove the condition expression.

cliSteps.command: aws dynamodb put-item --table-name fa-dynamodb-orders --item file://order-2001.json --condition-expression "attribute_not_exists(customerId) AND attribute_not_exists(orderId)" --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-dynamodb
cliSteps.explanation: This writes the third order under a different partition key.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command succeeds with no response body.
cliSteps.warning: Use only the harmless supplied data.

cliSteps.command: aws dynamodb get-item --table-name fa-dynamodb-orders --key "{"customerId":{"S":"CUSTOMER#100"},"orderId":{"S":"ORDER#1001"}}" --consistent-read --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-dynamodb
cliSteps.explanation: GetItem uses the complete primary key. --consistent-read requests the latest committed value from the base table.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The Item object contains ORDER#1001 with status PENDING.

verification.title: Confirm the item count
verification.instruction: Scan the small training table and inspect Count.
verification.expectedResult: Count is 3 and ScannedCount is 3.

verification.title: Confirm typed attributes
verification.instruction: Expand ORDER#1001 in JSON view.
verification.expectedResult: customerId, orderId, createdAt, status, and description are strings; amount and itemCount are numbers.

verification.title: Confirm an exact key read
verification.instruction: Retrieve CUSTOMER#100 plus ORDER#1001.
verification.expectedResult: Only the intended order is returned.

tasks.title: Perform safe updates with condition expressions
tasks.goal: Update an order only when its current status matches the expected value, then observe a deliberately rejected stale update.
tasks.whyItMatters: Conditional writes prevent lost updates and enforce business rules without a separate locking server.

consoleSteps.title: Update the order through the PartiQL editor
consoleSteps.instruction: Open DynamoDB in eu-west-2.

instructions.text: Open DynamoDB in eu-west-2.
Choose PartiQL editor in the left navigation.
Choose the fa-dynamodb-orders table.
Enter the supplied conditional UPDATE statement.
Choose Run.
Return to Explore table items.
Query CUSTOMER#100 and ORDER#1001.
Confirm status is PROCESSING and version is 2.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: ORDER#1001 is updated exactly once and retains all unrelated attributes.
consoleSteps.warning: The WHERE clause includes the complete key and expected current status; never run an unbounded update.

consoleSteps.title: Recognize the rejected stale update
consoleSteps.instruction: Run the same conditional UPDATE statement a second time.

instructions.text: Run the same conditional UPDATE statement a second time.
Read the error without changing the statement.
Return to Explore table items and retrieve ORDER#1001 again.
Confirm the item still shows status PROCESSING and version 2.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The second update changes no item because PENDING is no longer the current status.
consoleSteps.warning: A failed condition is expected in this test; it is not permission failure or data loss.

cliSteps.command: aws dynamodb update-item --table-name fa-dynamodb-orders --key "{"customerId":{"S":"CUSTOMER#100"},"orderId":{"S":"ORDER#1001"}}" --update-expression "SET #s = :next, #v = :version" --condition-expression "#s = :current" --expression-attribute-names "{"#s":"status","#v":"version"}" --expression-attribute-values "{":next":{"S":"PROCESSING"},":version":{"N":"2"},":current":{"S":"PENDING"}}" --return-values ALL_NEW --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-dynamodb
cliSteps.explanation: This atomic update changes the status only if the stored status is still PENDING.
cliSteps.expectedResult: Attributes in the response show status PROCESSING and version 2.
cliSteps.warning: Run it only once before the deliberate rejection test.

cliSteps.command: aws dynamodb update-item --table-name fa-dynamodb-orders --key "{"customerId":{"S":"CUSTOMER#100"},"orderId":{"S":"ORDER#1001"}}" --update-expression "SET #s = :next" --condition-expression "#s = :current" --expression-attribute-names "{"#s":"status"}" --expression-attribute-values "{":next":{"S":"SHIPPED"},":current":{"S":"PENDING"}}" --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-dynamodb
cliSteps.explanation: This deliberately stale update expects PENDING after the first update already changed the item.
cliSteps.expectedResult: DynamoDB returns ConditionalCheckFailedException and does not change the item.
cliSteps.warning: This error is expected. Do not weaken or remove the condition.

cliSteps.command: aws dynamodb get-item --table-name fa-dynamodb-orders --key "{"customerId":{"S":"CUSTOMER#100"},"orderId":{"S":"ORDER#1001"}}" --consistent-read --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-dynamodb
cliSteps.explanation: A strongly consistent read verifies that the rejected write did not alter the item.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The item still has status PROCESSING and version 2.

verification.title: Verify the accepted update
verification.instruction: Read ORDER#1001 after the first update.
verification.expectedResult: status is PROCESSING and version is 2.

verification.title: Verify rejection safety
verification.instruction: Read the same item after the deliberately stale update.
verification.expectedResult: The values remain PROCESSING and 2; no partial write occurred.

tasks.title: Compare Query, Scan, LSI, and GSI access patterns
tasks.goal: Retrieve orders through the base key, the customer time index, and the status index, then contrast those operations with Scan.
tasks.whyItMatters: SAA-C03 questions often reward key-based Query designs and penalize large table scans. GSIs support alternate partition keys; LSIs keep the base partition key and must be created with the table.

consoleSteps.title: Query the base table by customer
consoleSteps.instruction: Open Explore table items and select fa-dynamodb-orders.

instructions.text: Open Explore table items and select fa-dynamodb-orders.
Choose Query.
Select Table as the target.
Enter CUSTOMER#100 as customerId.
Leave the orderId sort-key condition empty.
Choose Run.
Inspect Count and the two returned order IDs.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The base-table Query returns ORDER#1001 and ORDER#1002 without reading the other customer partition.
consoleSteps.warning: Query requires an equality condition for the target partition key.

consoleSteps.title: Query the LSI and GSI
consoleSteps.instruction: Change the query target to customer-createdAt-index.

instructions.text: Change the query target to customer-createdAt-index.
Enter CUSTOMER#100 as customerId.
Choose Between for createdAt.
Choose Run and confirm both CUSTOMER#100 orders are returned in createdAt order.
Change the query target to status-createdAt-index.
Enter PENDING as status.
Choose Run.
Confirm ORDER#2001 is returned; ORDER#1001 is absent because its status is now PROCESSING.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The LSI answers a time-ordered query within one customer, while the GSI answers a cross-customer status query.
consoleSteps.warning: GSI reads are eventually consistent; a recent status change may take a short time to appear.

consoleSteps.title: Run a small Scan and compare its counters
consoleSteps.instruction: Change the operation to Scan.

instructions.text: Change the operation to Scan.
Add a filter where status equals PENDING.
Choose Run.
Inspect Count and ScannedCount.
Compare the scan counters with the GSI Query result.
Record that a filter is applied after items are read.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: Count is smaller than or equal to ScannedCount, demonstrating that a Scan filter does not avoid the underlying reads.
consoleSteps.warning: This three-item Scan is for learning only; avoid full-table scans for high-volume request paths.

cliSteps.command: aws dynamodb query --table-name fa-dynamodb-orders --key-condition-expression "customerId = :c" --expression-attribute-values "{":c":{"S":"CUSTOMER#100"}}" --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-dynamodb
cliSteps.explanation: This Query targets one base-table partition.
cliSteps.expectedResult: Count is 2 and the response contains ORDER#1001 and ORDER#1002.

cliSteps.command: aws dynamodb query --table-name fa-dynamodb-orders --index-name customer-createdAt-index --key-condition-expression "customerId = :c AND createdAt BETWEEN :start AND :end" --expression-attribute-values "{":c":{"S":"CUSTOMER#100"},":start":{"S":"2026-08-14T09:00:00Z"},":end":{"S":"2026-08-14T09:30:00Z"}}" --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-dynamodb
cliSteps.explanation: The LSI reuses customerId and orders matching items by createdAt.
cliSteps.expectedResult: Count is 2 and items are ordered by createdAt.

cliSteps.command: aws dynamodb query --table-name fa-dynamodb-orders --index-name status-createdAt-index --key-condition-expression "#s = :status" --expression-attribute-names "{"#s":"status"}" --expression-attribute-values "{":status":{"S":"PENDING"}}" --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-dynamodb
cliSteps.explanation: The GSI supports an alternate partition key across customers.
cliSteps.expectedResult: ORDER#2001 is returned; if propagation is still occurring, retry after a short wait.
cliSteps.warning: Do not add --consistent-read because GSIs do not support strongly consistent reads.

cliSteps.command: aws dynamodb scan --table-name fa-dynamodb-orders --filter-expression "#s = :status" --expression-attribute-names "{"#s":"status"}" --expression-attribute-values "{":status":{"S":"PENDING"}}" --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-dynamodb
cliSteps.explanation: Scan reads the table before applying the status filter.
cliSteps.expectedResult: Count is the number returned after filtering and ScannedCount shows how many items were evaluated.
cliSteps.warning: Use Scan only because this training table is deliberately tiny.

verification.title: Verify the base access pattern
verification.instruction: Query CUSTOMER#100 on the base table.
verification.expectedResult: Exactly two orders are returned.

verification.title: Verify the LSI rule
verification.instruction: Inspect customer-createdAt-index.
verification.expectedResult: It uses customerId like the base table but replaces the sort key with createdAt.

verification.title: Verify the GSI rule
verification.instruction: Inspect status-createdAt-index.
verification.expectedResult: It uses status as an alternate partition key and createdAt as its sort key.

verification.title: Verify Scan cost behavior
verification.instruction: Compare Count with ScannedCount.
verification.expectedResult: The filter changes returned items but does not reduce items evaluated by the Scan.

tasks.title: Enable Time to Live and mark an item for future expiry
tasks.goal: Enable the expiresAt TTL attribute and add a valid epoch-seconds value without waiting for deletion.
tasks.whyItMatters: TTL removes expired items asynchronously without consuming write capacity, making it useful for sessions, caches, and temporary records.

consoleSteps.title: Enable TTL on the exact attribute name
consoleSteps.instruction: Open fa-dynamodb-orders.

instructions.text: Open fa-dynamodb-orders.
Choose the Additional settings tab.
Find Time to Live (TTL).
Choose Turn on.
Enter expiresAt with the exact capitalization shown.
Choose Turn on TTL.
Wait until the TTL section shows Enabling or Enabled.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: TTL is configured to read epoch seconds from expiresAt.
consoleSteps.warning: TTL can take about one hour to become Enabled. Do not submit the enable action repeatedly.

consoleSteps.title: Add a future expiry to one harmless item
consoleSteps.instruction: Open Explore table items.

instructions.text: Open Explore table items.
Select fa-dynamodb-orders.
Query CUSTOMER#200 and ORDER#2001.
Choose the returned item and choose Edit item.
Add a Number attribute named expiresAt.
Enter 2147483647 as its value.
Choose Save changes.
Hover over or inspect expiresAt and confirm it represents a future date.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: ORDER#2001 contains expiresAt as a Number while the other orders remain unchanged.
consoleSteps.warning: TTL deletion is asynchronous and can occur days after expiry. This lab uses a future value so the item remains available for later tasks.

cliSteps.command: aws dynamodb update-time-to-live --table-name fa-dynamodb-orders --time-to-live-specification Enabled=true,AttributeName=expiresAt --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-dynamodb
cliSteps.explanation: This tells DynamoDB which case-sensitive Number attribute contains epoch seconds.
cliSteps.expectedResult: TimeToLiveSpecification shows Enabled true and AttributeName expiresAt.
cliSteps.warning: Run this once; UpdateTimeToLive is not idempotent during the transition.

cliSteps.command: aws dynamodb update-item --table-name fa-dynamodb-orders --key "{"customerId":{"S":"CUSTOMER#200"},"orderId":{"S":"ORDER#2001"}}" --update-expression "SET expiresAt = :expiry" --expression-attribute-values "{":expiry":{"N":"2147483647"}}" --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-dynamodb
cliSteps.explanation: The item receives a valid future epoch-seconds TTL value.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command succeeds without changing the primary key or order status.

cliSteps.command: aws dynamodb describe-time-to-live --table-name fa-dynamodb-orders --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-dynamodb
cliSteps.explanation: This verifies the TTL state independently of item data.
cliSteps.expectedResult: AttributeName is expiresAt and status is ENABLING or ENABLED.
cliSteps.warning: Do not wait for this training item to be deleted.

verification.title: Verify the TTL configuration
verification.instruction: Inspect the TTL section or run describe-time-to-live.
verification.expectedResult: The configured attribute is exactly expiresAt.

verification.title: Verify the item attribute type
verification.instruction: Inspect ORDER#2001.
verification.expectedResult: expiresAt is stored as Number 2147483647, not as a formatted date string.

verification.title: Understand asynchronous expiry
verification.instruction: Confirm the item remains visible during the lab.
verification.expectedResult: Remaining visible is expected because the value is in the future and TTL is asynchronous.

tasks.title: Enable DynamoDB Streams and inspect change records
tasks.goal: Capture both old and new images for an item update and inspect the stream metadata without deploying consumer code.
tasks.whyItMatters: DynamoDB Streams drives event-based processing with Lambda and supports audit, replication, and materialized-view patterns.

consoleSteps.title: Enable a stream with old and new images
consoleSteps.instruction: Open fa-dynamodb-orders.

instructions.text: Open fa-dynamodb-orders.
Choose the Exports and streams tab.
Find DynamoDB stream details.
Choose Turn on.
Select New and old images.
Choose Turn on stream.
Record the displayed stream ARN as [STREAM_ARN].

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The table shows an enabled stream with view type NEW_AND_OLD_IMAGES.
consoleSteps.warning: Stream records expire after 24 hours; this is not a permanent audit log.

consoleSteps.title: Generate one change and inspect the table result
consoleSteps.instruction: Open Explore table items.

instructions.text: Open Explore table items.
Query CUSTOMER#100 and ORDER#1002.
Choose Edit item.
Change status from SHIPPED to DELIVERED.
Choose Save changes.
Return to the Exports and streams tab.
Confirm the stream remains enabled and its ARN is unchanged.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: ORDER#1002 is DELIVERED and a corresponding stream modification record is available to consumers.
consoleSteps.warning: The DynamoDB Console shows stream configuration, not a full record browser; use the CLI inspection route for raw stream records.

cliSteps.command: aws dynamodb update-table --table-name fa-dynamodb-orders --stream-specification StreamEnabled=true,StreamViewType=NEW_AND_OLD_IMAGES --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-dynamodb
cliSteps.explanation: This enables change records containing the item images before and after each modification.
cliSteps.expectedResult: TableDescription.LatestStreamArn is populated.

cliSteps.command: aws dynamodb update-item --table-name fa-dynamodb-orders --key "{"customerId":{"S":"CUSTOMER#100"},"orderId":{"S":"ORDER#1002"}}" --update-expression "SET #s = :delivered" --expression-attribute-names "{"#s":"status"}" --expression-attribute-values "{":delivered":{"S":"DELIVERED"}}" --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-dynamodb
cliSteps.explanation: This generates one MODIFY event after the stream is enabled.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command succeeds and the GSI is updated asynchronously.

cliSteps.command: aws dynamodbstreams list-streams --table-name fa-dynamodb-orders --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-dynamodb
cliSteps.explanation: This returns the active stream descriptor.
cliSteps.expectedResult: Record the StreamArn as [STREAM_ARN].

cliSteps.command: aws dynamodbstreams describe-stream --stream-arn [STREAM_ARN] --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-dynamodb
cliSteps.explanation: This lists stream shards and the key schema.
cliSteps.expectedResult: StreamDescription.StreamStatus is ENABLED; record the first ShardId as [SHARD_ID].
cliSteps.warning: Replace [STREAM_ARN] with the exact value returned in the previous step.

cliSteps.command: aws dynamodbstreams get-shard-iterator --stream-arn [STREAM_ARN] --shard-id [SHARD_ID] --shard-iterator-type TRIM_HORIZON --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-dynamodb
cliSteps.explanation: This requests a temporary iterator starting at the oldest retained record.
cliSteps.expectedResult: Record ShardIterator as [SHARD_ITERATOR].
cliSteps.warning: Shard iterators expire quickly; use the returned value promptly.

cliSteps.command: aws dynamodbstreams get-records --shard-iterator [SHARD_ITERATOR] --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-dynamodb
cliSteps.explanation: This retrieves retained records from the selected shard.
cliSteps.expectedResult: A MODIFY record shows OldImage status SHIPPED and NewImage status DELIVERED, or an empty page if a different shard was selected.
cliSteps.warning: If the page is empty, inspect other listed shards rather than inventing a record.

verification.title: Verify stream configuration
verification.instruction: Inspect the table stream details.
verification.expectedResult: Status is enabled and view type is NEW_AND_OLD_IMAGES.

verification.title: Verify change generation
verification.instruction: Read ORDER#1002.
verification.expectedResult: The current status is DELIVERED.

verification.title: Verify stream semantics
verification.instruction: Inspect a MODIFY record when available.
verification.expectedResult: Keys identify ORDER#1002 and the record includes old and new images.

tasks.title: Enable PITR, create an on-demand backup, and restore it
tasks.goal: Protect the orders table, create a named backup, and prove recovery by restoring a separate table.
tasks.whyItMatters: PITR protects against accidental writes or deletes within a recovery window, while on-demand backups provide named recovery points without affecting table performance.

consoleSteps.title: Enable point-in-time recovery and create a backup
consoleSteps.instruction: Open fa-dynamodb-orders.

instructions.text: Open fa-dynamodb-orders.
Choose the Backups tab.
In Point-in-time recovery, choose Edit.
Enable point-in-time recovery.
Keep the default recovery period unless the Console requires a selection.
Save the change.
In On-demand backups, choose Create backup.
Enter fa-dynamodb-orders-backup.
Choose Create backup.
Wait until the backup status is Available.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: PITR is enabled and fa-dynamodb-orders-backup is Available.
consoleSteps.warning: Backups and restored table storage can incur charges until they are deleted.

consoleSteps.title: Restore the on-demand backup into a separate table
consoleSteps.instruction: On the Backups tab, select fa-dynamodb-orders-backup.

instructions.text: On the Backups tab, select fa-dynamodb-orders-backup.
Choose Restore.
Enter fa-dynamodb-orders-restore as the new table name.
Keep Europe (London) as the destination Region.
Keep the restored index and encryption settings.
Choose Restore table.
Open Tables and select fa-dynamodb-orders-restore.
Wait until its status is Active.
Choose Explore table items and run a Scan on the restored table.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: fa-dynamodb-orders-restore is Active and contains the backed-up harmless orders.
consoleSteps.warning: A restore always creates a new table; it does not overwrite fa-dynamodb-orders.

cliSteps.command: aws dynamodb update-continuous-backups --table-name fa-dynamodb-orders --point-in-time-recovery-specification PointInTimeRecoveryEnabled=true --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-dynamodb
cliSteps.explanation: This enables continuous point-in-time protection for the table.
cliSteps.expectedResult: PointInTimeRecoveryDescription.PointInTimeRecoveryStatus is ENABLED.

cliSteps.command: aws dynamodb create-backup --table-name fa-dynamodb-orders --backup-name fa-dynamodb-orders-backup --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-dynamodb
cliSteps.explanation: This creates a named on-demand backup without pausing the table.
cliSteps.expectedResult: Record BackupDetails.BackupArn as [BACKUP_ARN].
cliSteps.warning: Keep the exact ARN because the restore and cleanup commands require it.

cliSteps.command: aws dynamodb restore-table-from-backup --target-table-name fa-dynamodb-orders-restore --backup-arn [BACKUP_ARN] --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-dynamodb
cliSteps.explanation: This restores the named backup into a separate table.
cliSteps.expectedResult: TableDescription.TableStatus is CREATING.
cliSteps.warning: Replace [BACKUP_ARN] with the exact ARN returned by create-backup.

cliSteps.command: aws dynamodb wait table-exists --table-name fa-dynamodb-orders-restore --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-dynamodb
cliSteps.explanation: This waits for the restored table to become Active.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The waiter exits successfully.

cliSteps.command: aws dynamodb scan --table-name fa-dynamodb-orders-restore --select COUNT --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-dynamodb
cliSteps.explanation: A count-only Scan confirms that items were restored.
cliSteps.expectedResult: Count is greater than zero and matches the backed-up sample set.
cliSteps.warning: Use this only on the tiny restored training table.

verification.title: Verify PITR
verification.instruction: Inspect Backups or describe continuous backups.
verification.expectedResult: Point-in-time recovery status is ENABLED.

verification.title: Verify the on-demand backup
verification.instruction: Inspect fa-dynamodb-orders-backup.
verification.expectedResult: Backup status is AVAILABLE and its source table is fa-dynamodb-orders.

verification.title: Verify the restore boundary
verification.instruction: Compare the source and restored table names.
verification.expectedResult: fa-dynamodb-orders remains intact and fa-dynamodb-orders-restore is a separate Active table.

verification.title: Verify restored data
verification.instruction: Run a count against fa-dynamodb-orders-restore.
verification.expectedResult: The restored table contains the training items.

tasks.title: Create and test a Global Tables replica
tasks.goal: Add an eu-west-1 replica, write one harmless item there, and verify it appears in eu-west-2.
tasks.whyItMatters: Global Tables provide managed multi-Region, multi-active replication for low-latency access and regional resilience.

consoleSteps.title: Add the Ireland replica
consoleSteps.instruction: Open fa-dynamodb-orders in Europe (London).

instructions.text: Open fa-dynamodb-orders in Europe (London).
Choose the Global tables tab.
Choose Create replica.
Select Europe (Ireland) eu-west-1.
Review that the replica will use the same table name fa-dynamodb-orders.
Acknowledge that DynamoDB may create its account-shared AWSServiceRoleForDynamoDBReplication service-linked role when the first Global Table is created.
Choose Create replica.
Wait until both Europe (London) and Europe (Ireland) show Active.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: fa-dynamodb-orders is a Global Table with Active replicas in eu-west-2 and eu-west-1.
consoleSteps.warning: The second replica incurs storage and replicated-write charges. Complete the verification promptly and remove it during cleanup. Do not delete the shared DynamoDB service-linked role.

consoleSteps.title: Write in Ireland and verify in London
consoleSteps.instruction: Change the Console Region to Europe (Ireland) eu-west-1.

instructions.text: Change the Console Region to Europe (Ireland) eu-west-1.
Open DynamoDB and choose Explore table items.
Select fa-dynamodb-orders.
Choose Create item and JSON view.
Paste the supplied replica-test item JSON.
Choose Create item.
Change the Console Region back to Europe (London) eu-west-2.
Open fa-dynamodb-orders and query CUSTOMER#GLOBAL plus ORDER#GLOBAL1.
Retry after a short wait if replication has not appeared yet.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The item written in eu-west-1 is visible in eu-west-2 without an application-managed replication process.
consoleSteps.warning: Always check the Region selector before writing or deleting a replica resource.

cliSteps.command: aws dynamodb update-table --table-name fa-dynamodb-orders --replica-updates Create={RegionName=eu-west-1} --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-dynamodb
cliSteps.explanation: This adds Europe (Ireland) as a replica of the existing table. DynamoDB may create its shared AWSServiceRoleForDynamoDBReplication service-linked role if the account does not already have it.
cliSteps.expectedResult: TableDescription.Replicas contains eu-west-1 with a creating status.
cliSteps.warning: Replica creation can take several minutes and incurs charges. Do not delete the shared DynamoDB service-linked role during lab cleanup.

cliSteps.command: aws dynamodb wait table-exists --table-name fa-dynamodb-orders --region eu-west-1 --profile fa-dynamodb
cliSteps.explanation: This waits until the Ireland replica exists.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The waiter exits successfully.

cliSteps.command: aws dynamodb put-item --table-name fa-dynamodb-orders --item file://global-replica-test-item.json --condition-expression "attribute_not_exists(customerId) AND attribute_not_exists(orderId)" --region eu-west-1 --profile fa-dynamodb
cliSteps.explanation: Save the displayed replica-test JSON, then write it specifically in Ireland.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The write succeeds in eu-west-1.
cliSteps.warning: Confirm --region eu-west-1 before running this command.

cliSteps.command: aws dynamodb get-item --table-name fa-dynamodb-orders --key "{"customerId":{"S":"CUSTOMER#GLOBAL"},"orderId":{"S":"ORDER#GLOBAL1"}}" --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-dynamodb
cliSteps.explanation: This reads the replicated item from the original London replica.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response contains the REPLICATED item after propagation completes.
cliSteps.warning: If the first response is empty, retry after a short wait.

verification.title: Verify both replica states
verification.instruction: Inspect the Global tables tab.
verification.expectedResult: eu-west-2 and eu-west-1 both show Active.

verification.title: Verify cross-Region replication
verification.instruction: Read CUSTOMER#GLOBAL and ORDER#GLOBAL1 in eu-west-2.
verification.expectedResult: The item written in eu-west-1 is returned.

verification.title: Verify the SAA-C03 boundary
verification.instruction: Review that Global Tables are multi-active rather than a read-only replica design.
verification.expectedResult: Either Region can accept writes and DynamoDB resolves replicated updates.

tasks.title: Inspect monitoring, capacity, consistency, and architecture choices
tasks.goal: Use real table settings and metrics to choose between DynamoDB designs without creating extra chargeable services.
tasks.whyItMatters: The exam tests workload fit: on-demand versus provisioned, strong versus eventual reads, DynamoDB versus relational databases, Global Tables, backups, Streams, DAX, and S3.

consoleSteps.title: Inspect table monitoring and capacity settings
consoleSteps.instruction: Return to Europe (London) eu-west-2.

instructions.text: Return to Europe (London) eu-west-2.
Open fa-dynamodb-orders.
Choose the Monitor tab.
Inspect Successful request latency, Throttled requests, Read usage, and Write usage.
Set a recent time range that includes this lab activity.
Confirm there are no unexplained sustained throttles.
Choose Additional settings.
Find Read/write capacity and confirm On-demand is selected.
Do not switch capacity mode during this lab.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The learner can locate operational metrics and confirm the table uses on-demand request billing.
consoleSteps.warning: CloudWatch metrics can take several minutes to appear.

consoleSteps.title: Review security and resilience settings
consoleSteps.instruction: Inspect Encryption details and confirm encryption at rest is enabled.

instructions.text: Inspect Encryption details and confirm encryption at rest is enabled.
Inspect Point-in-time recovery and confirm it is enabled.
Inspect DynamoDB stream details and confirm NEW_AND_OLD_IMAGES.
Inspect Global tables and confirm both Regions.
Review the table ARN and confirm the training IAM policy limits access to fa-dynamodb- names.
Do not enable Contributor Insights or create DAX because they are not required for this small lab and can add cost.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The learner can point to the table controls for encryption, recovery, event capture, and multi-Region resilience.
consoleSteps.warning: DynamoDB encrypts all table data at rest; a customer-managed KMS key is optional and was not created here.

consoleSteps.title: Apply the exam decision rules
consoleSteps.instruction: Choose DynamoDB for serverless key-value or document workloads requiring predictable low-latency access at scale.

instructions.text: Choose DynamoDB for serverless key-value or document workloads requiring predictable low-latency access at scale.
Choose Query with a suitable key or index instead of Scan for high-volume request paths.
Choose on-demand capacity for unpredictable traffic and provisioned with auto scaling for steadier predictable traffic.
Choose strongly consistent base-table reads when the latest committed value is required in one Region.
Remember that GSI and Global Tables reads are eventually consistent.
Choose PITR for accidental-change recovery and Global Tables for multi-Region availability.
Choose Streams with Lambda for event-driven reactions to item changes.
Choose DAX when a read-heavy workload needs an in-memory DynamoDB-compatible cache.
Choose RDS or Aurora when joins, relational constraints, or complex SQL transactions are the primary requirement.
Choose S3 rather than DynamoDB for large objects; store object metadata or keys in DynamoDB.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The learner has a practical SAA-C03 decision checklist tied to settings used in the lab.
consoleSteps.warning: These are architecture selection rules, not instructions to create additional services.

cliSteps.command: aws dynamodb describe-table --table-name fa-dynamodb-orders --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-dynamodb
cliSteps.explanation: This supplies the live table status, indexes, stream ARN, replicas, size, and billing details.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The table is ACTIVE and includes the expected indexes, stream, and eu-west-1 replica.

cliSteps.command: aws cloudwatch list-metrics --namespace AWS/DynamoDB --dimensions Name=TableName,Value=fa-dynamodb-orders --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-dynamodb
cliSteps.explanation: This lists available DynamoDB metrics for the exact table without creating an alarm.
cliSteps.expectedResult: Metric entries include the fa-dynamodb-orders TableName dimension when data is available.
cliSteps.warning: Metrics may appear after a short delay.

cliSteps.command: aws dynamodb describe-continuous-backups --table-name fa-dynamodb-orders --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-dynamodb
cliSteps.explanation: This confirms recoverability independently of the Console.
cliSteps.expectedResult: PointInTimeRecoveryStatus is ENABLED.

cliSteps.command: aws dynamodb describe-time-to-live --table-name fa-dynamodb-orders --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-dynamodb
cliSteps.explanation: This confirms lifecycle configuration.
cliSteps.expectedResult: AttributeName is expiresAt and status is ENABLING or ENABLED.

verification.title: Verify no sustained throttling
verification.instruction: Inspect ThrottledRequests for the lab time range.
verification.expectedResult: No unexplained sustained throttling is present.

verification.title: Verify the capacity decision
verification.instruction: Inspect the current billing mode.
verification.expectedResult: The unpredictable beginner lab uses PAY_PER_REQUEST.

verification.title: Verify recovery and replication
verification.instruction: Inspect PITR and Global Tables.
verification.expectedResult: PITR is enabled and the Ireland replica is Active.

verification.title: Verify architecture understanding
verification.instruction: Explain when Query, GSI, PITR, Streams, Global Tables, DAX, RDS, and S3 are appropriate.
verification.expectedResult: Each service or feature is matched to its intended workload rather than selected by habit.

tasks.title: Remove only the DynamoDB training resources
tasks.goal: Delete every resource created by this Follow Along without touching any pre-existing table, identity, policy, backup, or profile.
tasks.whyItMatters: Complete cleanup controls cost, protects unrelated resources, and demonstrates operational ownership.

consoleSteps.title: Remove the replica, restored table, backup, and source table
consoleSteps.instruction: Sign in as fa-dynamodb-user and select Europe (London) eu-west-2.

instructions.text: Sign in as fa-dynamodb-user and select Europe (London) eu-west-2.
Open fa-dynamodb-orders and choose the Global tables tab.
Select only the Europe (Ireland) eu-west-1 replica.
Choose Delete replica and confirm the exact table and Region.
Wait until eu-west-1 is no longer listed as a replica.
Open Tables and select only fa-dynamodb-orders-restore.
Choose Delete and confirm fa-dynamodb-orders-restore.
Wait until fa-dynamodb-orders-restore is absent from Tables.
Open Backups and select only fa-dynamodb-orders-backup.
Choose Delete and confirm the backup name.
Open Tables and select only fa-dynamodb-orders.
Choose Delete and confirm fa-dynamodb-orders.
Refresh Tables and confirm neither training table is listed.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The replica, restored table, backup, and source table are no longer present.
consoleSteps.warning: Read every confirmation dialog. Never select a table or backup without the fa-dynamodb- prefix.

consoleSteps.title: Switch to the administrator and remove the temporary IAM identity
consoleSteps.instruction: Sign out of fa-dynamodb-user.

instructions.text: Sign out of fa-dynamodb-user.
Sign in with the same administrator-capable identity used for bootstrap.
Open IAM and choose Users.
Open fa-dynamodb-user.
Choose Security credentials.
Delete the access key recorded as [FA_DYNAMODB_ACCESS_KEY_ID].
Choose Permissions.
Detach fa-dynamodb-training-policy.
Return to Users and delete fa-dynamodb-user.
Open Policies.
Search for fa-dynamodb-training-policy.
Delete only fa-dynamodb-training-policy.
Confirm the user and policy no longer appear.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The temporary access key, policy attachment, IAM user, and customer-managed policy are removed.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not delete the administrator identity or any policy not created by this lab.

consoleSteps.title: Remove only the local named profile
consoleSteps.instruction: Open the .aws folder in the current Windows user profile.

instructions.text: Open the .aws folder in the current Windows user profile.
Back up the credentials and config files before editing them.
Open the credentials file in a text editor.
Remove only the [fa-dynamodb] section and its lines.
Open the config file in a text editor.
Remove only the [profile fa-dynamodb] section and its lines.
Save both files.
Leave every other profile unchanged.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The named profile fa-dynamodb is gone and unrelated AWS CLI profiles remain unchanged.
consoleSteps.warning: The credentials section and config section have different headings; remove exactly the two named sections.

cliSteps.command: aws dynamodb update-table --table-name fa-dynamodb-orders --replica-updates Delete={RegionName=eu-west-1} --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-dynamodb
cliSteps.explanation: This removes the chargeable Ireland replica before the source table.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response shows the replica deletion transition.
cliSteps.warning: Confirm RegionName is eu-west-1.

cliSteps.command: aws dynamodb wait table-not-exists --table-name fa-dynamodb-orders --region eu-west-1 --profile fa-dynamodb
cliSteps.explanation: This waits for replica removal to finish.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The waiter exits successfully.

cliSteps.command: aws dynamodb delete-table --table-name fa-dynamodb-orders-restore --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-dynamodb
cliSteps.explanation: This deletes only the restored training table.
cliSteps.expectedResult: TableDescription.TableStatus is DELETING.

cliSteps.command: aws dynamodb wait table-not-exists --table-name fa-dynamodb-orders-restore --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-dynamodb
cliSteps.explanation: This waits until the restored table is gone.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The waiter exits successfully.

cliSteps.command: aws dynamodb delete-backup --backup-arn [BACKUP_ARN] --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-dynamodb
cliSteps.explanation: This deletes only fa-dynamodb-orders-backup using its recorded ARN.
cliSteps.expectedResult: BackupDescription.BackupDetails.BackupStatus changes to DELETED or the backup disappears.
cliSteps.warning: Verify the ARN contains table/fa-dynamodb-orders/backup before running.

cliSteps.command: aws dynamodb delete-table --table-name fa-dynamodb-orders --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-dynamodb
cliSteps.explanation: Deleting the source table also removes its indexes, TTL setting, PITR setting, and stream configuration.
cliSteps.expectedResult: TableDescription.TableStatus is DELETING.

cliSteps.command: aws dynamodb wait table-not-exists --table-name fa-dynamodb-orders --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-dynamodb
cliSteps.explanation: This waits until the source table is fully gone.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The waiter exits successfully.

cliSteps.command: aws iam delete-access-key --user-name fa-dynamodb-user --access-key-id [FA_DYNAMODB_ACCESS_KEY_ID] --profile [ADMIN_PROFILE]
cliSteps.explanation: After switching back to the administrator, this invalidates the temporary key.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command returns without error.
cliSteps.warning: Do not run this through the fa-dynamodb profile after its key is removed.

cliSteps.command: aws iam detach-user-policy --user-name fa-dynamodb-user --policy-arn arn:aws:iam::<ACCOUNT_ID>:policy/fa-dynamodb-training-policy --profile [ADMIN_PROFILE]
cliSteps.explanation: This removes the managed-policy attachment before deleting the user and policy.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command returns without error.

cliSteps.command: aws iam delete-user --user-name fa-dynamodb-user --profile [ADMIN_PROFILE]
cliSteps.explanation: The administrator deletes only the temporary training user.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command returns without error.

cliSteps.command: aws iam delete-policy --policy-arn arn:aws:iam::<ACCOUNT_ID>:policy/fa-dynamodb-training-policy --profile [ADMIN_PROFILE]
cliSteps.explanation: The administrator deletes only the customer-managed training policy.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command returns without error.

cliSteps.command: aws configure list --profile fa-dynamodb
cliSteps.explanation: Run this before manual file editing to identify the exact local profile entries that will be removed.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The output identifies the fa-dynamodb profile sources.
cliSteps.warning: AWS CLI has no single profile-delete command; remove the exact sections manually as instructed in the Console route.

verification.title: Verify DynamoDB cleanup
verification.instruction: List tables in eu-west-2 and eu-west-1.
verification.expectedResult: fa-dynamodb-orders and fa-dynamodb-orders-restore are absent in both Regions.

verification.title: Verify backup cleanup
verification.instruction: List backups and search for fa-dynamodb-orders-backup.
verification.expectedResult: The named training backup is absent.

verification.expectedResult: fa-dynamodb-user and fa-dynamodb-training-policy are absent.

warnings.cost: DynamoDB tables, PITR, backups, restored tables, and the eu-west-1 Global Tables replica can incur charges. Use only the tiny supplied data and complete the final cleanup.

steps.title: Delete fa-dynamodb-orders replica in eu-west-1
steps.instruction:
Console:
- Open fa-dynamodb-orders in eu-west-2.
- Open Global tables.
- Select only the eu-west-1 replica.
- Choose Delete replica.

findings.message: Before candidate creation, confirm the Console labels against the current DynamoDB and IAM interfaces and keep the exact resource-name and Region safeguards.
The Global Tables task intentionally creates a chargeable eu-west-1 replica; confirm the cost warning and reverse-order removal remain prominent.

DynamoDB may create the account-shared AWSServiceRoleForDynamoDBReplication service-linked role for the first Global Table. It is not lab-exclusive, carries no standalone charge, and must be retained rather than deleted by this cleanup.
IAM-user credentials are used only for explicit training. For production workloads, prefer federation for people and IAM roles with temporary credentials for applications.
